q2: WITH e1 AS ( SELECT b1.name AS bar1, s.bar AS bar2, s.beer FROM serves AS s CROSS JOIN bar AS b1 ), e2 AS ( SELECT e1.bar1, e1.bar2, e1.beer FROM e1 EXCEPT SELECT e1.bar2 AS bar1, e1.bar1 AS bar2, e1.beer FROM e1 ) SELECT e2a.bar2 AS bar1, e2a.bar1 AS bar2 FROM e2 AS e2a EXCEPT SELECT e2.bar1, e2.bar2 FROM e2;
explanation: The difference between Q1 and Q2 lies in the way they handle bars serving the exact same set of beers versus those with different sets. Q1 identifies pairs of bars where one serves more beers than the other or have the same set. In contrast, Q2 focuses on pairs of bars with asymmetrically served beers, where one has a beer that the other does not and vice versa, leading to potentially no output in some cases.
